review_text: April 2026 — I visited around 2:00 PM after grabbing lunch at Nanyang nearby. This is the second Starbucks branch in the SM City Davao complex, located on the first level of the SM Expansion Wing (the other being the newly renovated Annex branch). The aesthetic is a beautiful take on elevated Filipino design, featuring cushioned seats, wooden tables, ample space, warm lighting, and minimalist wall decor. However, despite the inviting ambiance, nearly every spot was taken by people on laptops with notebooks, pens, and bags sprawled across the tables. I noticed a row of cushioned seats on the right where only a few people were sitting, yet the surrounding empty seats were completely covered in their personal belongings. By 3:00 PM, which is peak coffee hour, a queue had formed with nowhere for new customers to sit. It’s frustrating to see tables meant for 4 to 5 people occupied by only two, with extra chairs rendered unusable because they are being used as luggage racks. I even had to ask a guy if I could use a chair he was using as a footrest. While the service was fast, only one cashier was on duty and no printed receipts were available. Starbucks is known for its "Third Place" policy, but I feel it occasionally cultivates a culture of taking up too much space without regard for others. In Bisaya, we call this behavior "dalok" which means an unwillingness to share, and in this case, chairs and tables in a communal shop.
